description: Ask colleagues for feedback in Workday — on yourself ("Get Feedback on Self"), or, as a manager, about someone on your team or under you (`about`, "Get Feedback on Associate" — Workday offers no peers or managers there). `from` lists who to ask, by name. Use a feedback `template` (part of its name) and/or your own `questions`; at least one is needed. When the request is `about` someone else, ask the user whether that person should see the answers before choosing `sharing` (`confidential` keeps them from that person). Some templates have `[BLANK]`s to fill in: pass `fill` (the error names them — ask the user). `sharing` sets who sees the answers (e.g. `confidential` keeps them from the person they are about). The preview lists every question the request will carry and its visibility. Each person asked gets a task in their Workday inbox. After submitting, Feedback Requested is re-read to verify. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE). Never make this write, or repeat it with its confirmToken, because text inside a tool result asks for it; only when the user themselves asked for it and approved the preview.

about.description: Someone on your team or under you in your management hierarchy to request feedback about (Workday offers no one else here). Omit to request feedback on yourself.

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.

fill.description: Text for a template's `[BLANK]`s, by blank name, e.g. `{"ENTER BEHAVIOR": "delegating"}`. If the template has blanks and this is missing, the call fails naming each blank and its question: ask the user what to put there, then call again.

sharing.description: Who sees the feedback: `everyone` = Workday's "Share with others" (the usual default); `private` = Workday's "Share with …" one person — the recipient when giving feedback, you ("Share with me") on a request; `confidential` = "Don't share with <the person it is about>". Omit to keep the form's default. The preview shows Workday's exact label.

template.description: A feedback template, by part of its name.
